clue.text: Right steal

blocks.note: first meaning: suitable, proper (adjective)
second meaning: to take for oneself without permission (verb)

explanation.walkthrough: Two words with no link: one spelling, two pronunciations, an adjective and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means fitting or proper; the verb means to seize something that belongs to someone else.

clue.text: Does sewer have those? It's an uncomfortable feeling

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: a sewer here is one who sews, whose kit holds sharp metal implements
second meaning: the tingling felt as a numb limb wakes up

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what lurks in a drain, then admits the thought is unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as a drain, but it is someone who sews (rhymes with 'grower').
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for the prickling sensation of returning circulation, and literally the tools of a needleworker.

clue.text: Reportedly track origin

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so the word wanted is one that sounds like the next one

blocks.note: a track is a course or way, said with the 'oo' pronunciation

explanation.surface: A report into where a particular trail began.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of something is its source or basis, the place it grows from.

clue.text: Document I don't know on drink

blocks.note: what a quiz contestant says when stumped
fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs at what a document says, perhaps after a drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official travel document proving identity and nationality.

clue.text: Flowers in roses I rightly pulled up

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit inside the run of words that follows
in a down clue, pulling something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the end of the first word, the lone letter and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A gardener decides to uproot some roses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' could be a river (things that flow), but here it is plainly the blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are garden plants with showy blooms, so they are examples of flowers.

clue.text: Fish in a fruitcake brought over

indicators.note: bringing something over turns it the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
both are slang for an eccentric or crazy person

explanation.surface: A fruitcake turns up with an unexpected fishy ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' is not the baked goods but slang for a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish, often canned, so it is an example of fish.

clue.text: Better than hint, obviously faultless?

blocks.note: to be above something is to surpass it
a suspicion of something is a trace or slight hint of it

explanation.surface: Someone better than merely hinted-at is plainly innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond suspicion is so clearly innocent that nobody could doubt their honesty.

clue.text: Use river with bit of salt water

blocks.note: the Wear is a river in north-east England flowing through Durham
'with' and 'and' both join things together
a teardrop is a drop of salty water from the eye

explanation.surface: Someone makes use of a river where it meets the briny sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear and tear is the gradual damage caused by ordinary use over time, so the noun phrase means use.

clue.text: Abhorrent conclusion, bane evil

indicators.note: something evil is corrupt or twisted, so the preceding letters are bent out of shape

blocks.note: the two words, letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A disgusting ending, a wicked curse: a jumble of gloomy words.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconscionable conduct is so unreasonable or immoral that it is outrageous and morally repugnant.

clue.text: Performance I saw with very hot dancing

indicators.note: letters that dance move about and change places

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spectator recalls a show featuring some steamy dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety show is a stage or TV entertainment made up of several different acts, so it is a kind of performance.

clue.text: Absent, a system

blocks.note: taken as written
a way of doing something is a method or system

explanation.surface: A register note: absent, a whole system down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone away is not present, elsewhere for the time being.

clue.text: Power maintained by top sportsperson in race

indicators.note: something maintained by another is held and supported within it

blocks.note: a seeded player is one ranked among the best in a tournament
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A leading athlete keeps up the power during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is used as a verb: to go very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed is to move fast or hurry, the same as to race along.

clue.text: Opener removed from fielding position for spell of bowling

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, and that is taken away

blocks.note: cover is a fielding position on the off side in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket captain drops the opening batsman from the field to bowl a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' sounds like a cricket batsman but simply means a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by one bowler, a spell of bowling.

clue.text: A camp, out of the way

blocks.note: taken as written
a camp is a faction or party, one side in a dispute

explanation.surface: A campsite pitched somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' suggests tents, but here it means a faction in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put aside is moved to one side, out of the way.

clue.text: Serious amount?

blocks.note: first meaning: flagrant
second meaning: twelve dozen, 144

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one question about a large sum; the adjective and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross means glaring or serious in law, and as a noun it is a count of twelve dozen items.

clue.text: In little bits, railway business

blocks.note: taken as written
dust is tiny particles
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A railway company falling apart piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry is manufacturing or commercial activity, a branch of trade or business.

clue.text: Nick is residing in flat, briefly

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, so its last letter goes
something residing in another lives inside it

blocks.note: lying flat, face down
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Nick lives in a small apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name, but it is British slang for a jail; 'flat' is not a home but lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nick is a police station or jail, where offenders are locked up.

clue.text: What begins with a beat, pal improvising around Beethoven's Fifth

indicators.note: improvising means making things up freely, so the letters get rearranged
the fifth of a word is its fifth letter
the rearranged letters go around the selected letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the composer's name, fifth letter kept

explanation.surface: A musician jams around a Beethoven symphony, starting from the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifth' suggests the symphony, but it means the fifth letter of the composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet, the ordered set of letters, starts with the letter a.

clue.text: In test, put a stop to breaks

indicators.note: one thing breaking another splits it open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: a try is an attempt or trial
to end something is to stop it

explanation.surface: Someone halts the breaks during an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition but is the definition: fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in is currently fashionable, the same as trendy.

clue.text: Tightly packed store cleared out in secret

indicators.note: a word cleared out has its contents emptied, leaving just its outside letters
the emptied word goes inside the next one

blocks.note: closet as an adjective means secret, hidden
the word's first and last letters

explanation.surface: A crammed store is emptied out on the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' and 'secret' swap expected roles: the store is emptied, and secret gives the cupboard word.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-set describes things placed near together, such as close-set eyes, so tightly packed.

clue.text: Possible breakfast TV show announced?

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word wanted only needs to sound right

blocks.note: a television drama broadcast in episodes

explanation.surface: A broadcaster announces a new breakfast-time programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal such as cornflakes is a typical morning meal, so a possible example of breakfast.

clue.text: Soft drink: I'm going without one on the counter

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped
read as running counter, against the normal direction

blocks.note: Spanish farewell, what you say when leaving
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bar customer leaves a fizzy drink unfinished on the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' paints a bar top but means going against the direction of reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water and sweet fizzy pop are both non-alcoholic carbonated beverages.

clue.text: Last of all in kingdom, prince without biggish debts, solvent

indicators.note: the last of every word that follows is taken, its final letter

blocks.note: final letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A prince free of large debts is, at last, solvent in his realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solvent' looks like the prince is out of debt; here it is a liquid that dissolves things.
explanation.definitionFit: Meths, short for methylated spirits, is an alcohol-based liquid used as a cleaning solvent and fuel.

clue.text: Narcissist keen to make a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way you came, so read the word backwards

blocks.note: eager, enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A self-obsessed star is eager for a return to fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a temperamental, self-important star, so the word is used of a vain, self-absorbed person.

clue.text: Tongue held by paramour, dutifully

indicators.note: the letters wanted are held inside the following words

blocks.note: end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A lover obediently keeps a kiss going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' suggests a kiss, but means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, and tongue is another word for a language.

clue.text: Dope working for government department

blocks.note: a machine that is in is running
the Foreign Office, a UK ministry

explanation.surface: A drug dealer is employed in a ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs or a fool; it is slang for inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for information or the inside story, and info is short for information.

clue.text: Mentioned a drab drunk that will pick your pocket in Vegas?

definitions.text: that will pick your pocket in Vegas?

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreary drunk who picks pockets in a Las Vegas casino.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: no thief, but a machine that takes your money.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit machine, named for its lever and its habit of taking gamblers' money, is a casino fixture.

clue.text: Item on list, killer objective

blocks.note: a bullet is what kills when a gun is fired
the point of something is its aim or purpose

explanation.surface: An assassin's to-do list with its target written down.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet point is a marked entry in a list, so it is an item on a list.
